items.title: 1. My Brain Feels Damaged: your bleed lines first, mine after in plain words
items.where: If Someone Says "My Brain Feels Damaged": DMSO + Humic Acid + Electrolytes First, P12
items.my_version: If someone is worried about a bleed, I'd probably skip DMSO, but it depends on how severe their issue is. It's not a powerful blood thinner like heparin, unless maybe injected; it's basically a dietary blood thinner. I've never had any issues with bleeding too much from consuming DMSO, and never heard of it either, but if bleeding is already a medical issue I'd want to think about that more. They can feel better on DMSO with a clot or a bleed still there. So if any of the checks above fail, call medics right away, before the window for treating a stroke closes.
items.before: DMSO cannot identify whether the problem is a clot, a hemorrhage, low oxygen, an electrolyte crisis, or something else. The larger adjacent risk is losing a treatment window or missing a bleed because the symptoms improved enough to feel reassuring. items.title: 3. Serotonin Syndrome, step 2: cyproheptadine and how far its evidence goes
items.where: Do this immediately when serotonin toxicity is reasonably suspected:, P1
items.your_version: If the person is fully alert and able to swallow, I would give cyproheptadine early, since it blocks serotonin receptors. So far, the evidence for this med has only been case reports, and a recent review found them insufficient to show that it works. I wouldn't wait to see whether it does before doing the other steps.

items.title: 2. MDMA: what else to do once the jaw tenses, and which signs mean medics
items.where: MDMA: Jaw Tension Is the Magnesium Alarm, P5
items.your_version: Once their jaw tenses, that should be their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. If they drink a lot of plain water, even a single normal MDMA dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead. The following indicators would justify calling medics: If their confusion or headache worsens, or vomiting won't stop (sodium might be too low and it could be too late for an easy fix). If their muscles keep getting weaker or their heart palpitations keep getting stronger, that could be from dangerously low potassium, like my second wife had. A seizure or collapse can result from low potassium, and can also come from overheating or MDMA toxicity.

items.my_version: Jaw tension should also mean no more MDMA, less exertion and heat, and closer monitoring. Worsening headache, confusion, vomiting, weakness, palpitations, collapse, or seizure raises concern about sodium, potassium, temperature, hydration, kidneys, and broader toxicity. MDMA is documented to cause acute kidney injury through several pathways, and controlled research confirms that hyponatremia can occur after a single dose.
